name: Red-capped Robin
rangeDescription: Interior of southern australia, to southern and western coasts
description: Small Australian robin. Male black above, with a black head and chin, vivid scarlet breast and forecrown.

name: Lesser Grass-Finch
rangeDescription: Marshes of eastern paraguay to southeastern brazil and northeastern argentina
description: Large finch with a long spiky tail and strong yellow bill. It is yellow-brown above with dark lines running down the back and pale buff below with a gray face and a white throat.

name: Amazonian Scrub-Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to southern venezuela, the guianas, northern bolivia, and amazonian brazil
description: A confusing flycatcher, fairly small and nondescript. Look for the short bill and round head, sometimes raised into a slight crest.

name: Somali Grosbeak
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern somalia near ethiopian border
description: Handsome chunky gray-brown finch with a massive dark bill, dark-brown cap, and blackish face mask extending to the throat. Female has a paler forehead and crown.

name: Bananal Antbird
rangeDescription: Central brazil (bananal island and right bank of rio javaés, tocantins)
description: An antbird with a very restricted distribution in the Araguaia Valley. Males are black with white wing bars and white tips to the tail, while females are similar but gray and slightly streaked on the breast.

name: Cuban Blackbird
rangeDescription: Cuba including isla de la juventud (isle of pines; south of western cuba)
description: A vocal, gregarious inhabitant of many habitats, although avoids dense woods; often found near human habitation. Note the glossy purple-black plumage, medium-length squared tail, and somewhat thick bill.

name: Slaty Tanager
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru to western bolivia (la paz and cochabamba)
description: Large gray-and-red tanager of mid-elevation humid montane forest. Males are dark gray with a dark reddish orange crown; females are gray above and rusty orange below, with a white lower belly and eyebrow.

name: Alta Floresta Antpitta
rangeDescription: Amazonian brazil (south of the amazon river, between the madeira and the xingu)
description: Secretive species, almost tailless with long legs. Has a black-spotted breast, white throat, and conspicuous buff “goggles”.

name: Juan Fernandez Tit-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Robinson crusoe island (juan fernández islands, far off southern chile)
description: Restricted to Isla Robinson Crusoe in the Juan Fernandez Islands where no similar species occur. Uncommon and declining.

name: Brown Violetear
rangeDescription: Belize and guatemala to the guianas, brazil, and bolivia
description: Uncommon, rather large but drab, fairly short-billed hummingbird of tropical and subtropical forest and edge. Can be aggressive when defending flower patches from most other hummingbirds.

name: Pale Mountain-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Bougainville to guadalcanal and malaita (solomon islands)
description: A long-tailed pigeon with striking plumage contrast. Dark gray on the back and wings with an entirely white underside and tail.

name: Screaming Cowbird
rangeDescription: Eastern bolivia to paraguay, southern brazil, uruguay, and northern argentina
description: Medium-sized cowbird found at woodland edges, savannas, and agricultural areas. Both sexes are entirely black with a bluish iridescence, except for rufous feathers on the underwing, which are difficult to see.

name: Blue-throated Hillstar
rangeDescription: Andes of southwestern ecuador (cordillera de chilla-tioloma-fierro urcu, on the el oro/loja border)
description: This spectacular hummingbird was only discovered in 2017, and made headlines when it was described as a new species to science a year later. It is currently known only from one mountain in the Andes of southwestern Ecuador called Cerro de Arcos.

name: Little Crow
rangeDescription: Inland australia (reaching coasts in west and south)
description: Australian crows and ravens are challenging to identify; concentrate on call, throat-hackles, behavior, and location. Calls usually a very fairly short, repeated “ah-ah-ah.” Note relatively short bill, white bases to the small throat hackles.

name: Spot-winged Starling
rangeDescription: Foothills of northern india and nepal; winters to myanmar and thailand
description: Uncommon pale-eyed starling with a white patch on each wing. Male is metallic dark blue-gray above with an orange breast and belly.

name: St. Vincent Wren
rangeDescription: St. vincent (lesser antilles)
description: Small brownish wren found only on St. Vincent.

name: Humboldt Penguin
rangeDescription: Humboldt current region of coastal northern peru to southern chile
description: Uncommon and local; breeds in colonies along the coast of Peru and Chile, where it nests in underground burrows. The only penguin in most of its range, but some overlap in central Chile with similar Magellanic Penguin of colder southern waters.

name: Chestnut-quilled Rock-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Western escarpment of arnhem land (northern northern territory)
description: A large dark-brown pigeon with faint pale speckles on its plumage. In flight, shows chestnut wing panels, and flies with a loud clattering of wings.

name: Planalto Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Northeastern argentina (missiones) and far southern brazil (southwestern paraná to southern rio grande do sul)
description: Small, nondescript bird that is usually very difficult to spot. Mostly dark gray with a cinnamon vent with dark bars.

name: Ainley's Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: Winter breeder on islets off guadalupe island (western mexico); nonbreeding range poorly known, but apparently disperses south in eastern pacific, at least as far as the galapagos
description: Rare and poorly known seabird found in the Pacific Ocean well off the coast of Mexico. It breeds in the winter on small islets near Guadalupe Island, located 160 miles from the mainland, and disperses southward during other times of the year.
